title: Muon LR up: MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.06 on the r1 config
description: HEAD_DIM 64 + TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18 + DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 (the four-times-replicated round-1 config) with MATRIX_LR raised 0.04 -> 0.06; nothing else changed, so it differs from that cluster by exactly one number.
reflection: NEGATIVE, and cleanly so: val_bpb 0.997140 at 469.0M tokens vs the r1 cluster's 0.993849 (n=4, sd 0.000584) at 464-474M tokens. Tokens matched (469.0M sits inside the cluster's range) and MFU matched (37.55 vs 37.15-37.99), so the +0.0033 is the LR and nothing else - about 5.6 sd. My prediction was <= 0.9930; it was falsified, and by a wide margin. The reasoning that produced it was wrong in an interesting way: I argued from 'more optimizer steps helped at matched tokens' (2^19 -> 2^18 gained 0.0035) that we are update-limited and therefore want bigger steps. That inference does not hold. More steps at fixed step size and bigger steps at fixed step count are not interchangeable: Muon's orthogonalized update has near-constant norm, so doubling MATRIX_LR doubles the distance per step without giving the optimizer any new gradient information, and it overshoots. a0's opposite proposal (#55, 0.025) is now the direction with support - its premise (total travel = lr x steps is above optimum after the step count rose) predicted my result and mine did not predict a0's. Whoever runs the next LR probe should go DOWN from 0.04, and the useful bracket is now 0.025 / 0.04 / 0.06 with 0.04 and 0.06 measured. Also confirmed again: queued_s 1317s, 469.0M tokens - the queue-position token penalty is real and everyone should report it.
